assessment.assessment: UCR stylistics, psycholinguistics and comparative literature teach general methods for analysing language and narrative. World Myth & Literature uses Greek, Roman and Near Eastern narratives, but the active courses do not build Hebrew grammar, original Hebrew source interpretation or a sequence in Hebrew literary traditions.

World Archaeology includes the ancient Near East, and philosophy, cultural history and historical methods can help study religion, diaspora and material culture. They do not sustain the degree’s study of Jewish communities, rabbinic sources, Jewish intellectual history or modern Jewish societies.

assessment.concept: Middle Eastern History, Society and Politics
assessment.assessment: Global history, comparative politics, conflict analysis, Mediterranean visual culture and international law support regional questions and methods. They do not provide cumulative study of Middle Eastern history, society, religion and politics or the region-specific research progression of the named major.

distinctness: No UCR option was selected. Trial differences do not establish a disciplinary match.
